# Checkpoint R external follow-up — next documentary target after Folder 10

Date: 2026-09-12
Branch: `claude/k4-post-j`

Folder 10 (`Pre-Production and Notes, 1990-1999`) has now been inspected from the complete user-supplied image batch and was negative for cipher-panel geometry / K4 method. Do not ask a future agent to re-audit it.

## Recommended next low-contamination target

**Jim Sanborn papers — Series 9: Scrapbooks — Box 16, Folder 2 — `Kryptos Sculpture, circa 1975-1993`.**

Official AAA page:

`https://www.aaa.si.edu/collections/jim-sanborn-papers-22298/series-9/box-16-folder-2`

Series page:

`https://www.aaa.si.edu/collections/jim-sanborn-papers-22298/series-9`

AAA describes Series 9 as scrapbooks containing clippings, announcements, photographs, and some correspondence. Folder 16/2 is specifically titled `Kryptos Sculpture, circa 1975-1993` and includes additional scrapbook pages and loose material.

### Why this outranks `Codes Research`

The current unresolved documentary question is physical/fabrication geometry: straight-on or production-era imagery showing row starts, letter spacing, pitch, alignment, or construction state. A Kryptos-specific scrapbook with photographs is a safer next source for that narrow question than Box 6 Folder 11 `Codes Research`, which has materially greater contamination risk and is more likely to contain solution-adjacent cryptographic material.

### What to look for if obtained

Priority items:

- straight-on or orthographic photographs of the cipher panel
- installation/fabrication photographs before curvature obscures alignment
- close-ups showing row starts/ends and character spacing
- photographs of templates, transfer sheets, punches, stencils, or shop layouts
- correspondence explicitly discussing how text was physically laid out

Do not infer a common lattice from oblique publicity photographs alone.

## Contamination rule

If any scrapbook item contains or reproduces alleged K4 plaintext, a solution method, or private solution material, quarantine it and do not use it cryptanalytically. Public construction photographs, clippings, and fabrication correspondence are safe.

K4 remains unsolved.
